title: Personal Checking: Bank-Error Refunds of Overdraft Protection Transfer Fees
content:
## What this policy governs

On a Personal Checking account, an overdraft protection transfer fee that was charged against the charter is the bank's own error, and the bank gives it back as a bank-error correction. The obligation arises from what the account's records show; it does not wait for the customer to ask. The business outcome is a single refund entry against the fee in question, or no refund at all where the fee turns out to have been charged properly. A goodwill request about a properly charged fee is a separate matter for the courtesy refund rules.

## Observable effect

Once the refund is posted, it appears in the account activity straight away, it is recorded as a bank-error correction of an overdraft protection transfer fee, and the posted ledger balance goes up by the refunded sum at that moment.

## The refund tool

`refund_transfer_fee_error_033d9cbf` is a hidden tool that the agent operates: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. Each call books exactly one refund entry dated today against one overdraft protection transfer fee entry, as a full bank-error correction. The tool takes the values it is given at face value; it does not examine the fee, its date, its amount or whether it was refunded before.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `checking_account_id` | reference number of the checking account the fee was charged to, as the checking account lookup returns it | identifier |
| `customer_id` | customer reference number of the account's owner, as the customer profile lookup returns it | identifier |
| `source_item_id` | reference number of the overdraft protection transfer fee entry that is being refunded, as shown in the account activity | identifier |
| `amount` | the refund in U.S. dollars | positive plain number with two decimal places, rounded half-up (for instance 12.34) |
| `statement_cycle` | the statement cycle into which today's posting falls | `YYYY-MM`, the month in which that cycle closes |

### Return

On success the tool replies with a single sentence of confirmation. That sentence identifies the refund entry just created and the transfer fee entry it reverses, and states two dollar figures, each to the cent: the sum refunded and the posted ledger balance the account now shows. Its arrival is the sign that the refund is posted.
